articles.snippet:
Mistlabs launched Ambi, an ambient intelligence platform designed to reason in real time, anticipate user needs, and eventually enable communication between independent AI agents.
The post Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Mistlabs Launches Ambi Following $26 Million Funding Round To Advance Real-Time Ambient AI And AI-to-AI Communication
Mistlabs launched Ambi, an ambient intelligence platform designed to reason in real time, anticipate user needs, and eventually enable communication between independent AI agents.
The launch follows $26 million in Pre-A funding led by Luminous Ventures and Huaqin Technology.
Mistlabs said the financing will support development of its standalone AI wearable in addition to continued expansion of the Ambi platform.
Ambi is launching out of beta on Apple devices and is currently designed to work across the iPhone, Apple Watch, Mac, and MacBook.
Mistlabs describes Ambi as a system that goes beyond traditional AI summarization and task completion by continuously building contextual understanding of a user throughout the day.
The platform is designed to identify opportunities to act proactively rather than waiting for a direct prompt.
Ambi retains information about users’ preferences, priorities, communication style, and work patterns in memory, allowing its understanding to carry across supported devices.
The company said this persistent context allows Ambi to provide recommendations, identify missing information, flag irregularities, and continue working on projects even when the user is no longer actively focused on them.
One of Ambi’s features, called Routine, allows multiple agents to perform recurring tasks.
For example, during a meeting discussing competitors, Ambi can analyze and fact-check the conversation in real time while simultaneously researching competing products and preparing information for a follow-up proposal.
Mistlabs said Ambi can also continue evaluating a project after a meeting has ended and proactively flag new developments or issues that may require attention.
The company plans to expand the system further through agent-to-agent communication.
Under that model, individual Ambi agents would be able to communicate with one another on behalf of their respective users, subject to permissions granted by those users.
During meetings, the agents could identify overlapping priorities, surface areas of disagreement, and potentially suggest mutually acceptable outcomes as discussions take place.
Mistlabs said this capability is intended to allow AI systems to act not only as assistants but also as collaborators or mediators.
The company plans to introduce agent-to-agent communication in the coming months.
Mistlabs is also developing its own wearable AI hardware designed specifically around Ambi.
The company said the wearable is intended to give Ambi a richer understanding of the user and surrounding context beyond what is available through existing devices.
Ambi is currently designed with privacy considerations that include not storing audio by default.
Mistlabs said its broader strategy is to move beyond AI systems focused primarily on one-off prompts, task management, and summarization toward continuously available contextual intelligence.
The company is headquartered in San Francisco and is led by CEO Peter Mo.

articles.title: Wally Raises $25M to Give Members Unlimited Cleanings and Diagnostics for $249 a Year
articles.snippet: A dentist told Wally cofounder Tyler Burnett he needed eight fillings, and two second opinions later he learned seven of them were unnecessary. That experience, plus a front-row view of how dental billing works, pushed him to build a dental company with no insurance and a flat $249 annual price. Find out why he says the industry's business model works against patients, and how Wally plans to turn $25M into 100 locations by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network
articles.snippet:
Dan-O's Seasoning has secured a $25 million strategic investment from The Newcastle Network, marking the consumer-focused private equity firm's first investment in the food category.
The post Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Dan-O’s Seasoning Secures $25 Million Strategic Investment From The Newcastle Network
Dan-O’s Seasoning has secured a $25 million strategic investment from The Newcastle Network, marking the consumer-focused private equity firm’s first investment in the food category.
The Louisville, Kentucky-based seasoning company plans to use the capital to expand retail and online distribution, introduce additional product formats, and bring more of its products to consumers as it continues scaling nationally.
Dan-O’s was founded in 2015 by Dan Oliver, who initially sold an early version of the company’s Original seasoning blend at a local farmers market. The business has since expanded into a national brand sold through more than 22,000 retailers and online.
The company has also built a community of more than 15 million home cooks across its audience and social channels. Dan-O’s attributes a significant part of its growth to customers experimenting with its blends, sharing recipes, combining flavors, and using the products across a broad range of meals.
Founder Dan Oliver and CEO Phillip Crosby will continue leading the company following the investment.
For The Newcastle Network, the transaction represents the firm’s first move into food and supports a broader strategy of backing founder-led consumer brands that have developed strong communities before expanding distribution.
The firm sees an opportunity for emerging brands to take share from established food companies by combining product differentiation with direct relationships with consumers. Newcastle plans to support Dan-O’s with capital and operational expertise spanning data science, technology, and go-to-market execution.
Dan-O’s has grown from a farmers market business into one of the faster-growing seasoning brands in the U.S. Its products are positioned as flavor-focused alternatives to traditional herbs and spices, and the company plans to continue expanding into new formats while maintaining its focus on its existing consumer community.
The Newcastle Network’s broader portfolio includes footwear company Kizik, collectibles business Super7, pet brand Pet Life Unlimited, and now Dan-O’s Seasoning.
The investment gives Dan-O’s additional resources to expand its retail footprint, increase online availability, and develop new ways for consumers to use its seasoning products.
KEY QUOTES:
“The brands we’re most excited about don’t just sell products, they change behavior. Dan has built far more than a seasoning company. He’s created a platform that inspires millions of home cooks to experiment, create, and enjoy cooking more. That’s rare, it’s incredibly difficult to replicate, and it’s exactly the kind of business we’re looking to back as we build our food portfolio. The Dan-O’s investment is just the beginning.”
Chris Casgar, Managing Partner At The Newcastle Network
“I started out at a farmers market with one goal: get people to put some Dan-O’s on it, have fun in the kitchen, and make food they were excited to share. Our Fan-O’s took it from there. They started shakin’ it on everything, mixing flavors, creating their own recipes, and making Dan-O’s part of their own cooking stories. They’ve built this into something way bigger than me. articles.title: Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work
articles.snippet:
Melius has raised $25 million to expand its AI-powered creative operating system, including a $5 million seed round led by General Catalyst and a $20 million Series A led by CRV. Genius Ventures, Vine Ventures, and Anti Fund also participated.
The post Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
Melius Raises $25 Million To Expand AI Agents Lab For Creative Work
Melius has raised $25 million to expand its AI-powered creative operating system, including a $5 million seed round led by General Catalyst and a $20 million Series A led by CRV. Genius Ventures, Vine Ventures, and Anti Fund also participated.
The New York-based company plans to use the funding to grow its team, expand its go-to-market and sales organization, and continue building out its agents lab for creative work.
Melius provides creative teams with a shared operating system where teams of AI agents can handle much of the production work involved in developing creative assets. The company is designed to reduce the need for users to work across multiple disconnected generative AI tools or rely heavily on prompt engineering.
Melius was co-founded by CEO Joowon Kim, CTO Young Kim, and COO Arnav Ramu. Joowon Kim and Young Kim previously worked together at Ramp, while Ramu has experience as an entrepreneur as well as in software investing at Hg and investment banking at Guggenheim.
The company emerged from stealth in July 2026 and reached a seven-figure run rate less than three months later. Thousands of teams are now using Melius to build creative assets.
Melius is focused on automating work across images, video, and audio so creative professionals can spend more time developing ideas while AI agents handle more of the production process.
KEY QUOTES:
“Creative teams don’t have an idea-quantity problem; they have a resource problem. Generative AI made content cheap to produce, but using it still means prompt-engineering your way through a dozen different tools. We built Melius so teams of AI agents handle everything between an idea and the finished asset, so people can spend their time being creative instead of operating tools.”
Joowon Kim, Co-Founder And CEO Of Melius
“Watching Joowon, Young, and Arnav pivot and execute at speed showed exactly the kind of conviction and execution we look for in founders. While most generative AI tools for creative teams are single-purpose, a prompt box here, an editor there, Melius has now built a true operating system where agents can take a workflow from first draft to finished asset. As AI agents get more capable, that full-workflow is where the advantage will compound.”
Yuri Sagalov, Managing Director At General Catalyst
“From our very first meeting, Joowon, Young and Arnav have been obsessed with one thing: helping people create exactly what they imagine with AI. That kind of clarity attracts great people, and we’ve been super impressed by how quickly they’ve brought A+ talent onto the team. With years of trust from building together at Ramp and a bias toward shipping fast, they’re exactly the team to win this market.”
Veronica Orellana And Reid Christian, General Partners At CRV

articles.title: Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor
articles.snippet:
Furientis has raised $25 million in seed funding led by Benchmark and secured its first funded government contract, supporting development of a 100-mile-range interceptor vehicle intended for homeland defense.
The post Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Furientis Raises $25 Million Seed Funding And Secures First Department Of War Contract For 100-Mile Interceptor
Furientis has raised $25 million in seed funding led by Benchmark and secured its first funded government contract, supporting development of a 100-mile-range interceptor vehicle intended for homeland defense.
Benchmark General Partner Chetan Puttagunta is joining the company’s Board in connection with the financing.
The government contract is structured as a prototyping Other Transaction Agreement with the Department of War.
The financial value of the government award was not disclosed.
Under the agreement, Furientis will continue developing its interceptor and demonstrate the flight vehicle’s performance against Department requirements.
The Los Angeles-based defense technology company is focused on producing lower-cost defensive interceptors at significantly greater volumes than traditional missile production programs.
Furientis is designing its system around manufacturability from the beginning rather than optimizing only for maximum technical performance and then addressing production requirements later.
The company evaluates components based in part on whether they can be manufactured at a rate supporting 1,000 interceptor vehicles annually per factory.
Furientis is also targeting a final assembly process requiring less than one hour per interceptor.
Where appropriate, the company uses commercial off-the-shelf components rather than automatically specifying aerospace or military-grade parts.
It also manufactures important components internally, including solid rocket motors and seekers.
Furientis tests prototypes in the field on a roughly biweekly cadence, allowing the company to modify designs based on flight data rather than waiting through long conceptual development cycles.
The seed financing and government contract will support additional investment in vertically integrated manufacturing, expanded flight-test operations and hiring across engineering and manufacturing at the company’s Los Angeles operation.
Furientis was founded by Brody Franzen and Aris Simsarian.
KEY QUOTES:
“Furientis exists to resupply our critical deficiency in defensive munitions. Recent events have shown these threats are not theoretical, and the U.S. is genuinely running low on the systems that protect the American people. That is fundamentally a production and manufacturing problem, and it’s the one we built this company to solve.”
Brody Franzen, Co-Founder and CEO of Furientis
“Furientis is building truly remarkable technology with the aim of creating a platform that can scale rapidly with the lowest cost in the world. The team is comprised of some of the most talented propulsion, hardware, and software engineers in the world.”
Chetan Puttagunta, General Partner at Benchmark

articles.text:
Mojo Vision Secures $24.4 Million Government Award To Advance Micro-LED Displays And Domestic Manufacturing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Mojo Vision Secures $24.4 Million Government Award To Advance Micro-LED Displays And Domestic Manufacturing
Mojo Vision has received $24.4 million in additional U.S. government funding to advance its micro-LED platform, expand domestic manufacturing capabilities, and develop monolithic full-color microdisplays for near-eye augmented reality applications. The funding was awarded under an Other Transaction Authority agreement through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Policy. The package includes $20 million from the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program and $4.4 million from U.S. Army Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance.
Mojo said the award is the largest government funding package it has received to date.
The program will focus on developing ultra-bright monolithic microdisplays using Mojo’s proprietary quantum dot color conversion technology. The displays are intended to improve brightness and reliability while reducing size, weight, and power requirements for near-eye augmented reality systems used in defense applications.
Mojo expects the work to support equipment that gives warfighters improved situational awareness while reducing display system size and weight.
The program is also expected to advance the underlying technologies shared across Mojo’s broader product platform, including micro-LED technology, CMOS integration, and wafer-scale manufacturing.
Those technologies support both the company’s display products and its optical interconnect business. Mojo is developing its micro-LED platform for applications that include next-generation AI glasses and optical interconnects designed for AI computing infrastructure.
The company’s technology stack includes 300mm silicon architecture, GaN-on-silicon micro-LED emitters, photodetectors, proprietary quantum dots, custom micro-lens arrays, multicore fiber bundles, and proprietary software.
Mojo positions its platform as a scalable, manufacturing-ready architecture that can be configured for multiple applications while addressing conventional trade-offs involving brightness, size, bandwidth density, and power consumption.
The government program also supports a broader objective of strengthening domestic production of advanced microdisplays for defense applications. Microdisplays are used across systems including pilot heads-up displays, advanced night vision equipment, weapon optics, and unmanned platforms.
Mojo said the latest award will strengthen the manufacturing foundation underlying both its defense-oriented display products and commercial micro-LED technologies.
KEY QUOTES:
“This award accelerates our work to put ultra-bright, full-color displays into the hands of the warfighter and strengthen America’s ability to manufacture them. We built Mojo around a simple idea: the same micro-LED technology that changes how people see information can change how computing systems move data. This program strengthens the technology and manufacturing foundation behind both.”
Nikhil Balram, CEO Of Mojo Vision
